primary_secondary.note: Includes a literature mapping step, but the main contribution is a metric catalog evaluated with practitioners.

study_type.claude: Mixed methods (mapping study, metric catalog, survey and structured interviews)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (literature mapping, survey, structured interviews)

research_method.claude: Mapping study (241 papers, 178 after duplicates, 65 analysed, 99 factors); 12-metric catalog built with expert categorisation; evaluation via survey (4-point Likert plus open questions, 47 developers) and structured interviews (22); Grounded Theory open/axial coding plus descriptive statistics
research_method.nlm: Mixed methods: systematic literature mapping (178 papers, 65 relevant), survey of 47 developers, structured interviews with 22; 12-metric catalog with conceptual causal model
research_method.value: Mixed methods: literature mapping (241 papers retrieved, 178 after de-duplication, 65 analysed; 99 factors) to build a 12-metric catalog of mental health and productivity metrics with formulas; evaluation by survey (Likert and open questions, 47 developers) and structured interviews (22 of them), analysed with Grounded Theory open/axial coding and descriptive statistics
research_method.note: 241 retrieved papers and Likert/coding details reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; practitioners mostly from Brazil, companies from <9 to >500 employees; private sector 36, NGO 5, startup 3, public 2; 47 survey respondents, 22 interviewed
context.nlm: Industry; private 36, non-profit 5, startups 3, public 2, company sizes <9 to 500+; 47 survey respondents, 22 interviewed; networks in Brazil
context.value: industry; software practitioners recruited via professional networks (survey asks region of Brazil), mostly private sector (36; non-profit 5, startups 3, public 2), company sizes from <10 to >500 employees; 47 survey respondents, 22 also interviewed

ai_discussed.note: The QSI metric proposes AI sentiment/emotion analysis of developer communications as the measurement instrument; developers' doubts about AI reliability and surveillance are a finding.

remote_covid.note: Borderline: both report the participants' work model (in-person 22, hybrid 26, fully remote 16); the paper also links distributed/hybrid work to resource loss and weaker team interaction, but does not analyse results by work model.

data_window.note: Not stated by either; no survey/interview dates found.

cat_productivity.note: Work Capacity (completed vs. assigned story points), Number of Resolved Issues, Missed Tasks, plus perceived productivity (SVI, TVI).

cat_quality.note: No quality metric in the catalog; quality appears only in developers' definitions of productivity.

cat_collaboration.note: Quality of Social Interactions (negative interactions in communications) and Team Vision (peer rating of productivity and collaboration).

cat_satisfaction.note: Individual/team mental health metrics (WVI, WEC, TOV, QSI, ABS, MOT).

cat_activity.note: Number of Commits (development activity); LOC used as an example item in the survey.

cat_delivery.note: Both label WCA (and NotebookLM also NRI) 'Productivity / Delivery', but completed story points and resolved issues are Productivity metrics.

cat_devex.note: Both use 'DevEx' as a loose label for some metrics; the DevEx framework is not used.

cat_agile.note: Metrics operationalized for agile settings (story points, sprint retrospectives, Scrum Masters, sprint-cycle cadence), with non-agile alternatives; borderline since the catalog is declared workflow-agnostic.

cat_survey.note: Self-rated (SVI) and peer-rated (TVI) daily surveys in the catalog; Likert survey and interviews for evaluation.
